federal_funding_rules.name: 90 percent federal match for design, development, installation or enhancement
federal_funding_rules.summary: FFP at 90 percent is available for the design, development, installation or enhancement of a mechanized claims processing and information retrieval system only when CMS approves the APD before the state spends the funds. CMS approves the system described in the APD when it is likely to provide more efficient, economical and effective administration of the state plan and the conditions in 433.112(b)(1) through (22) are met.
conditions_examples: Meets the system requirements, standards and conditions, and performance standards in Part 11 of the State Medicaid Manual
HHS receives a royalty-free, non-exclusive, irrevocable license to software and documentation built with 90 percent FFP
Information in the system is safeguarded under 42 CFR Part 431 Subpart F
Modularity, alignment to the Medicaid Information Technology Architecture, industry standards, reuse, reporting and interoperability conditions (see 433.112(b) for the full list of 22)
federal_funding_rules.what_it_means_for_a_vendor: A state can buy a module with 90 cents of every dollar coming from CMS, but only inside an approved APD. The vendor's product has to fit the state's modular architecture, license terms and certification plan, or the state loses the match.

sources.label: CMS MES certification repository: conditions for enhanced funding

federal_funding_rules.name: 75 percent federal match for operations
federal_funding_rules.summary: CMS approves 75 percent FFP for system operations when the conditions of 433.112(b)(1) through (22) are met at the time of approval, the system has been operating continuously during the period claimed, and it provides both patient and provider profiles for program management and utilization review.
federal_funding_rules.what_it_means_for_a_vendor: Operations and maintenance revenue on a certified module carries a 75 percent match. Losing certification puts the state back to the regular administrative match, which is why states write certification outcomes into vendor contracts.

federal_funding_rules.name: Advance Planning Document prior approval and contract thresholds
federal_funding_rules.summary: States plan and get approval for ADP acquisitions through Planning APDs, Implementation APDs and annual or as-needed APD Updates. Prior approval is required when a state plans to acquire ADP equipment or services with FFP at the regular matching rate and total acquisition costs of $5,000,000 or more. Contracts must be submitted before execution when they are anticipated to exceed $6,000,000 (competitive) or $1,000,000 (noncompetitive) for software application development, and $20,000,000 (competitive) or $1,000,000 (noncompetitive) for hardware and COTS software, unless the state uses an exemption or an Acquisition Checklist.

thresholds.label: Prior approval, regular match, total acquisition cost
Contract submission, software application development, competitive
Contract submission, software application development, noncompetitive
Contract submission, hardware and COTS, competitive
Contract submission, hardware and COTS, noncompetitive

federal_funding_rules.what_it_means_for_a_vendor: A state RFP above these lines has an APD behind it and CMS has seen the plan. A noncompetitive award above $1 million needs CMS's sign-off on the contract, which is why sole-source state deals stall.

smc.name: Streamlined Modular Certification (SMC)
smc.summary: SMDL 22-001 sunset the Medicaid Enterprise Certification Toolkit and the Medicaid Eligibility and Enrollment Toolkit and replaced them with SMC for all MES projects initiated after publication. CMS cut required state-submitted artifacts from 29 to 7 and moved to outcomes: CMS-required outcomes tied to statute and regulation, state-specific outcomes for the state's own priorities, and metrics that show the outcomes hold continuously. The SMC guidance defines the review stages (operational readiness review and certification review) and the intake form used for every MES module including MMIS, E&E and EVV.

mes_modules.name: Medicaid Enterprise System modules
mes_modules.summary: The MES is the sum of the discrete IT systems or services a Medicaid agency uses to manage, monitor and administer the program. Functions include beneficiary eligibility and enrollment, care management, provider enrollment and payment, benefits management, data analytics and reporting, health information exchange, and fraud and abuse detection. The CMS certification repository organizes required outcomes and metrics by module.

sources.label: Medicaid.gov: Streamlining Medicaid Enterprise Systems templates

t_msis.name: T-MSIS reporting
t_msis.citation: Social Security Act section 1903(r)(1); SHO 18-008; SHO 25-002
t_msis.summary: States submit Medicaid and CHIP data to the Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System monthly. Compliance is a condition of FFP for state automated data systems under section 1903(r)(1). CMS runs business-rule reviews on each monthly submission and expects continuous data quality work.

mars_e.name: MARS-E for eligibility and enrollment systems
mars_e.summary: Required for a state's Medicaid and CHIP E&E systems to keep their Authority to Connect with CMS; recommended but not required for MMIS. Full record in authorization-paths.json (id mars_e).

cooperative_purchasing.name: NASPO ValuePoint Cloud and Software Solutions (2026 to 2036)
cooperative_purchasing.summary: The lead state of Utah awarded competitively solicited master agreements to 58 suppliers for cloud and software solutions and services. Master agreements are effective 2026-09-16; as of 2026-09-10, 54 of 58 were fully executed. The legacy Cloud Solutions portfolio (2016 to 2026; PaaS, IaaS and SaaS categories) expires 2026-09-15. A state, territory, political subdivision or other eligible entity buys under a Participating Addendum approved by its Chief Procurement Official; each addendum says which entities in the state may use it.
cooperative_purchasing.eligible_buyers: All 50 states, DC, the territories, their political subdivisions, institutions of higher education and other eligible entities, subject to a Participating Addendum and local law
cooperative_purchasing.how_a_vendor_uses_it: Hold a master agreement, or partner with a supplier that holds one (several are resellers or distributors), then confirm the target state has signed a Participating Addendum.

cooperative_purchasing.name: GSA Cooperative Purchasing Program
cooperative_purchasing.summary: State, local, regional and tribal governments and their instrumentalities (including institutions of higher education) may buy IT, law enforcement and security products, services and solutions through GSA Multiple Award Schedule contracts, under 40 U.S.C. 502(c). Related programs: Disaster Purchasing, the 1122 Program and Public Health Emergency purchasing.
cooperative_purchasing.eligible_buyers: State or local government as defined in 40 U.S.C. 502(c)(3)
cooperative_purchasing.how_a_vendor_uses_it: Hold a MAS contract with cooperative purchasing accepted on the eligible SINs (the IT category), then sell to the state directly under MAS terms.

sources.label: GSA: programs for state and local governments

demand_signals.name: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F)
demand_signals.summary: Impacted payers include state Medicaid and CHIP fee-for-service programs, Medicaid managed care plans and CHIP managed care entities, Medicare Advantage organizations and QHP issuers on the federally facilitated exchanges. Operational provisions took effect 2026-01-01; API development and enhancement requirements are due by 2027-01-01. Payers must also publicly report prior authorization metrics.
demand_signals.what_it_means_for_a_vendor: Every state Medicaid program and its MCOs is building or buying FHIR prior authorization, provider access and payer-to-payer APIs on a 2027 clock. That is a live requirement with a date, not a forecast.

sources.label: CMS: Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F)

demand_signals.name: Medicaid provisions of H.R. 1 (2025 reconciliation law)
demand_signals.summary: Expansion adults ages 19 to 64 must report 80 hours a month of community engagement (work, community service, half-time enrollment) or an exception. States must implement by 2026-12-31, or earlier through 1115 waivers. Eligibility redeterminations for expansion adults move to every six months; sources place the first affected renewals at renewals scheduled on or after 2026-12-31 (some summaries say starting 2027-01-01). CMS issued initial guidance 2025-12-08 and HHS implementation guidance was due 2026-06-01. Nebraska was the first state to implement the work requirement, on 2026-05-01.

dates.event: CMS initial guidance on community engagement requirements.
HHS implementation guidance due to states.
States must implement community engagement requirements.

demand_signals.what_it_means_for_a_vendor: Eligibility and enrollment systems in 41 expansion jurisdictions need work-verification, exemption handling and six-month renewal logic on a 2026 clock. That is the largest state E&E change since the ACA, and it runs through the APD and SMC process above.
